#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR imagemagick.cve-2018-5246..."
    # Execute the PoC to trigger the vulnerability
    /work/bin/magick montage /testcase/poc.pattern /dev/null
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/imagemagick
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR njs.cve-2022-27007..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/njs/build/njs /testcase/poc.js
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/njs
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR gpac.cve-2024-50664..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 500 -bo -bound -keep-utc -out /dev/null /testcase/poc9gpac
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/gpac
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"

    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"

fi

payload.bug_description: A malformed OpenEXR header can trigger an invalid memory read (segmentation fault / invalid pointer dereference) in internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/validation.c). During header parsing (internal_exr_parse_header / exr_start_read), memcmp is called on attribute data that has not been properly validated, allowing crafted input to cause a crash/undefined behavior (denial-of-service).

#!/bin/bash

# Build script for GPAC

# Set default CFLAGS if not set
CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:--O2}"

# Check if configure script exists
if [ -f ./configure ]; then
    chmod +x ./configure
    ./configure --static-build --extra-cflags="$CFLAGS" --extra-ldflags="$CFLAGS"
else
    echo "Configure script not found. Skipping configuration."
fi

# Clean previous builds
make clean || echo "No previous build to clean."

# Build with all available processors
make -j$(nproc)
payload.secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."

    # Handle git sub-modules
    if [[ -f .gitmodules || -f .gitmodule ]]; then
        echo "Detected git sub-modules - initialising/updating..."
        git submodule update --init --recursive
    else
        echo "No git sub-modules found - skipping update."
    fi

    # stdout: /dev/null
    # stderr: grep filters out "warning:" and lets everything else through
    if /usr/local/bin/compile \
         1>/dev/null \
         2> >(grep -Fv --line-buffered -e "warning:" -e "SyntaxWarning:" -e "WARNING:" >&2); then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR gpac.cve-2023-4754..."
    # TODO: Add commands to trigger the specific vulnerability
    # For now, it's a placeholder.
    /src/gpac/bin/gcc/MP4Box -dash 1000 /testcase/crash000394
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # Example: /out/fuzzer /testcase/poc_file
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/gpac
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/mruby/mruby/issues/4062
## Description:
Issue: mruby/mruby#4062
Title: Signed integer overflow in mrb_str_format
State: closed
Created by: clayton-shopify
Created at: 2018-06-25 15:27:56+00:00

Issue Body:
The check macro (in `/mrbgems/mruby-sprintf/src/sprintf.c`) contains an signed integer overflow in `bsize`:

```c
#define CHECK(l) do {\
/*  int cr = ENC_CODERANGE(result);*/\
  while ((l) >= bsiz - blen) {\
    bsiz*=2;\
    if (bsiz < 0) mrb_raise(mrb, E_ARGUMENT_ERROR, "too big specifier"); \
  }\
  mrb_str_resize(mrb, result, bsiz);\
/*  ENC_CODERANGE_SET(result, cr);*/\
  buf = RSTRING_PTR(result);\
} while (0)
```

`bsiz*=2` can become negative. However with `-O2` the `mrb_raise` is never triggered, since `bsiz` is a signed integer. Signed integer overflows are undefined behaviour and thus `gcc` removes the check.

This results in negative integers being passed to `mrb_str_resize`, which will set the string length without further checks. This can potentially result in a oversized string that allows to access arbitrary memory.

In our experiments building with `gcc` in version `5.4.0 20160609 (Ubuntu 5.4.0-6ubuntu1~16.04.9)` produces the vulnerable binary while `clang` generated a safe executable. 
 
```c
MRB_API mrb_value
mrb_str_resize(mrb_state *mrb, mrb_value str, mrb_int len)
{
  mrb_int slen;
  struct RString *s = mrb_str_ptr(str);

  mrb_str_modify(mrb, s);
  slen = RSTR_LEN(s);
  if (len != slen) {
    if (slen < len || slen - len > 256) { //check passes if len < 0
      resize_capa(mrb, s, len);
    }
    RSTR_SET_LEN(s, len); //string len is set to a large value
    RSTR_PTR(s)[len] = '\0';   /* sentinel */ //oob access
  }
  return str;
}

Additionally, the attacker could use this vulnerability to cause a denial of service (DoS) by crashing the application or making it unresponsive. This vulnerability poses a significant risk to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of systems running the affected software.
